findings.claim: In the host validation regex, the (\/.*)? path group is dead because before_validation strips everything from the first '/' before validation runs.

verifier.reason: app/models/embeddable_host.rb: the before_validation hook strips the scheme and then runs `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`, which removes everything from the first '/' before validation runs. So the `(\/.*)?` group in `validates_format_of` (line ~3) never matches anything in practice (the spec at spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb shows 'https://example.com/1234/45' becoming 'example.com').

findings.claim: The plural *_ids hydration branch in Store._hydrateEmbedded always deletes *_ids keys, even when no sub-collection was side-loaded. This leaves arrays of undefined and breaks plain ID-list attributes such as muted_category_ids.

verifier.reason: In store.js.es6:196-201, the new `_ids` branch maps every id through `_lookupSubType` and then runs `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. When no matching collection was side-loaded, `_lookupSubType` (157-187) returns undefined, so the id list is replaced by an array of undefined. The singular branch at 204-207 avoids this by deleting only when hydration succeeds. The `muted_category_ids` example is weak, because categories resolve from memory (163-164), but any other plain id list hits the bug.

findings.claim: Store._hydrateEmbedded drops IDs for embedded relationships when the side-loaded data uses a different root key, for example featured_user_badges with root :user_badges. This produces arrays of undefined.

verifier.reason: In store.js.es6:196-201, the new `_ids` branch maps each ID through `_lookupSubType`, which looks only at `root[pluralize(subType)]` (store.js.es6:168). If that key is missing, as with featured_user_badges whose root is :user_badges (user_serializer.rb:73), every lookup returns undefined, yet the code still writes the array of undefined and runs `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. The singular `_id` branch (lines 203-207) keeps the ID when nothing is found.

findings.claim: The migration indexes execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup without checking for an empty result. It raises IndexError when no matching site_settings row exists, such as on fresh installs or the test DB.

verifier.reason: At db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11, `execute(...)[0]['id']` runs with no row check. `embed_category` defaults to '' and is only stored in site_settings once someone changes it, so a fresh install or the test DB returns no rows, and PG::Result#[] raises IndexError before the `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 can run. The `embeddable_hosts` lookup at line 19 does check `cmd_tuples`, which shows the guard was left off this query.

findings.claim: The uncategorized_category_id lookup at line 15 of the migration uses the same unguarded [0] index on the query result and fails on a fresh database.

verifier.reason: Line 15 does index `[0]` without a guard, but it does not fail on a fresh database: migration 20131022045114_add_uncategorized_category.rb:17-18 always inserts the `uncategorized_category_id` setting, so this query returns a row. The real fresh-database crash is the `embed_category` lookup at create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11, which returns no rows and fails before line 15 is reached.

findings.claim: The file (the serializer) ends with an extra trailing blank line, which breaks CONTRIBUTING's no-trailing-blank-lines rule.

verifier.reason: app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:16 is an extra blank line after the closing `end` on line 15, added by the patch (change.patch:434). CONTRIBUTING.md:49 has no rule that names trailing blank lines; it says only "no trailing whitespaces, blank lines should have no spaces". The extra line is real, but it breaks that rule only if trailing whitespace is read to include it.

findings.claim: In rest.js.es6, type.replace('_', '-') replaces only the first underscore, so a type containing several underscores resolves to the wrong base path.

verifier.reason: At app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 the patch adds `type.replace('_', '-')`. A string pattern replaces only the first match, so a type with several underscores (e.g. 'a_b_c' → 'a-b_c') would not match a hyphenated ADMIN_MODELS entry and would get '/' instead of '/admin/'. No current entry in ADMIN_MODELS (line 1) has more than one hyphen, so this is a latent bug only.

findings.claim: embeddable_hosts.category_id is NOT NULL but has no foreign key, no existence check in the controller, and no dependent handling. Deleting a category leaves orphaned host rows.

verifier.reason: The migration declares `t.integer :category_id, null: false` with no foreign key (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] without checking the category exists, EmbeddableHost only has `belongs_to :category` and no validation, and app/models/category.rb never mentions embeddable hosts, so deleting a category leaves orphaned host rows that TopicEmbed later passes to PostCreator.

findings.claim: The migration backfill interpolates legacy host strings directly into raw SQL (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)) without quoting or parameter binding. A value containing a single quote aborts the migration.

verifier.reason: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 (added by the patch) builds the INSERT with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) from the split site_settings value, with no quoting or binds. A host string containing a single quote breaks the SQL and makes the migration fail.

findings.claim: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard. A missing host raises NoMethodError (500) instead of producing a validation error.

verifier.reason: In the before_validation block at app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8, `self.host.sub!` is called with no nil check. If the request has no host, app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 sets `host.host` to nil, and `host.save` (line 27) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of failing validation and reaching render_json_error.

findings.claim: A missing params[:embeddable_host] raises an exception in the controller instead of returning a validation error.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23-24 reads params[:embeddable_host][:host] without a nil guard or params.require, so a request with no embeddable_host key fails with NoMethodError on nil (a 500 error) before the model validation and render_json_error at line 30 can run.

findings.claim: After saving an embeddable host, the client sets host.category from the possibly-null local categoryId instead of the category_id returned by the server. The server defaults that value to uncategorized, so the UI shows a blank category until reload.

verifier.reason: In the patch's embeddable-host component save() (change.patch:57), host.category is set from Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')). categoryId starts as null (change.patch:28) and stays null for a new host when the admin leaves the category chooser on its default Uncategorized option. Meanwhile the server replaces a blank category_id with uncategorized_category_id (change.patch:274), so the client gets an undefined category and the badge shows blank until reload.

findings.claim: Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing and only re-renders show. The PUT customize/embedding route and the client saveChanges action that back it are therefore dead.

verifier.reason: Admin::EmbeddingController#update (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11) does the same thing as show: it re-serializes @embedding, which fetch_embedding builds, and saves nothing. The only caller is the saveChanges action (admin-embedding.js.es6), which sends update({}) with an empty body, and no template uses it: embedding.hbs only binds addHost and deleteHost. Hosts are saved separately through the embeddable-host component, so the PUT customize/embedding route is effectively dead code.

findings.claim: The new create/update/destroy and embedding show endpoints have no behavioural tests. The specs only assert subclassing of AdminController.

verifier.reason: The two new spec files only check that each controller subclasses Admin::AdminController (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7, spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7). No spec in the repo calls the create/update/destroy actions in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:4-17 or embedding#show/update in app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:4-10.

findings.claim: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first and then call methods on the result. An unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, lines 10 and 15 look up the host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, which returns nil for an unknown id. Neither method checks for nil: line 16 calls `host.destroy`, and line 23 (in save_host) calls `host.host=`, so both raise NoMethodError (a 500) instead of returning 404.

findings.claim: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests hosts, because Topic#expandable_first_post? dropped the host-presence check.

verifier.reason: The patch reduces Topic#expandable_first_post? to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, with no host check left (app/models/topic.rb:869, patch line 389). The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' (spec/models/topic_spec.rb, patch lines 868-871) creates no EmbeddableHost, but it passes only because the unsaved topic has no topic embed, so it no longer tests anything about hosts.

findings.claim: The contents of spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped.

verifier.reason: After the patch, spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1-4 contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1-27 contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators, so the two files' contents are swapped. Fabrication loads every file in spec/fabricators, so all the fabricators are still defined and tests behave the same; the problem is only the misleading file names.

findings.claim: Host validation accepts a port (e.g. example.com:8080), but record_for_host compares against uri.host, which excludes the port. Such stored hosts never match.

verifier.reason: The validation regex at app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 allows `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the before_validation hook at lines 6-7 strips only the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is saved with its port. record_for_host (lines 344-347) compares `lower(host)` against `URI(...).host`, which never includes a port, so a host saved with a port can never match.

findings.claim: The pretender GET /fruits/:id handler ignores the id and always returns fruits[0]. The store.find('fruit', 2) test therefore checks the wrong record and passes accidentally.

verifier.reason: The GET /fruits/:id handler at test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:226-228 ignores the id and always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]). The patched 'find embedded' test asks for store.find('fruit', 2) but expects colors [1,2], which belong to apple; banana's color_ids are [3]. So the test passes only because the handler returns the wrong record.

findings.claim: The migration uses def change with raw execute data moves and deletes the old settings. Rollback raises IrreversibleMigration and the old data cannot be recovered.

verifier.reason: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb (patch lines 535-565) moves the data with raw `execute` inside `def change`, then runs `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts','embed_category')`, and there is no `up`/`down` or `reversible` block. A rollback cannot recreate the deleted settings; under Rails 4.1.10 it fails because `execute` cannot be inverted, though it may stop with a TypeError at the `[0]['id']` lookup before reaching IrreversibleMigration.

findings.claim: The admin.embedding.edit locale key is never referenced.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `admin.embedding.edit: "edit"` at config/locales/client.en.yml:461 (patch line 461). Nothing in the repo references `embedding.edit`, and the edit button in admin/templates/components/embeddable-host.hbs uses only `icon="pencil"` with no label.

findings.claim: A spec context description contains the typo 'emeddable' instead of 'embeddable'.

verifier.reason: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1407 has `describe 'with an emeddable host' do`. The patch adds this line (change.patch:877) and misspells 'embeddable'.

findings.claim: The migration copies legacy host strings verbatim via raw SQL and bypasses the model's scheme/path normalization. Entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' never match record_for_host after the upgrade.

verifier.reason: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 inserts each legacy line unchanged with raw SQL, so the scheme/path stripping in the model's before_validation (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8) never runs. A stored 'http://eviltrout.com' will never equal URI(referer).host in `lower(host) = ?` (embeddable_host.rb:17), even though the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? accepted such entries by stripping `^https?://`.

findings.claim: Icon-only d-button elements (save, cancel, edit, delete) have no accessible labels or title attributes, and the needed i18n keys do not exist.

verifier.reason: In embeddable-host.hbs:148-156 (patch lines 148-156), the four d-buttons have only `icon` and `action`, with no `label` or `title`. d-button.js.es6:7-14 sets the title attribute only from `title` or `label`, so these buttons render with no title and no text. The i18n part is only partly right: the patch adds `admin.embedding.edit` but never uses it, it adds no save, cancel or delete keys for embedding, and generic `js.save`/`js.cancel` keys already exist (client.en.yml:240-242).

findings.claim: record_for_host lowercases the host column with lower(host) but does not downcase the input host. Mixed-case hosts such as http://EvilTrout.com/x fail to match.

verifier.reason: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb (patch lines 340-348), record_for_host compares lower(host) against uri.host without downcasing it. Ruby's URI keeps the host's case, so "EvilTrout.com" never equals the lowercased column, the lookup returns nil, and host_allowed? is false.

findings.claim: The serializer defines explicit id/host/category_id methods that only return object.<attr>, which duplicates what the attributes declaration already does.

verifier.reason: The claim is correct. In app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb (patch lines 419-433), `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` is followed by `def id`, `def host` and `def category_id`, and each one only returns `object.<attr>`. The `attributes` declaration already reads those values from the object, so the methods repeat it. The same pattern appears for `id` in embedding_serializer.rb (patch lines 442-447).

findings.claim: The code uses hash-rocket syntax ':with =>', which goes against CONTRIBUTING's Ruby 1.9 hash syntax rule.

verifier.reason: The new file app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 (patch line 332) has `validates_format_of :host, :with => /.../i`. That breaks the rule in CONTRIBUTING.md:52 to use Ruby 1.9 hash syntax (`{ a: 1 }` rather than `{ :a => 1 }`).

findings.claim: The inner 'if records.present?' check is redundant after val.present? and split.

verifier.reason: In the migration added by change.patch (patch lines 554-556), `val.present?` means val has at least one non-whitespace character, so `val.split("\n")` always returns a non-empty array and `records.present?` is always true. Even if records were empty, `records.each` would simply do nothing, so the inner check adds nothing.

findings.claim: Trailing \r and whitespace from the textarea are kept when legacy hosts are inserted in the migration.

verifier.reason: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:555-558 the migration splits the old setting on "\n" only and puts each raw `h` straight into an INSERT. Nothing strips the values, and raw SQL skips the EmbeddableHost before_validation cleanup, so any trailing \r or whitespace is stored. Such a host will then never match `lower(host) = ?` in app/models/embeddable_host.rb:347.

findings.claim: In store.js.es6, obj[k].map throws TypeError when a *_ids field is null or not an array.

verifier.reason: At store.js.es6:192, any key that matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with the trailing 's' goes to the branch that calls `obj[k].map(...)` at line 197, and nothing checks for null or for an array first. So a `*_ids` value that is null throws a TypeError (and a non-array without `.map` does too). The `hydrated || []` fallback on the next line runs too late to prevent this.

findings.claim: destroyRecord() has no .catch(popupAjaxError), so delete errors are swallowed.

verifier.reason: In the new app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 (patch lines 65-67), the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. The save path in the same file does have one (patch line 59), so when a delete fails the user sees no error.

findings.claim: The Embedding wrapper (OpenStruct with id 'default', plus its own controller, serializer, adapter and routes) and the plural _ids store hydration exist only to wrap a host list.

verifier.reason: The Embedding OpenStruct holds only `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:305-308), its `update` action just re-renders without changing anything (embedding_controller.rb:298-300), and EmbeddingSerializer only emits `id` plus `embeddable_host_ids` (app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:441-448). The new plural `_ids` hydration (discourse/models/store.js.es6:220-232) is used in the app only by that `embeddable_host_ids` key; the only other user is the fruit/colors test fixture.

findings.claim: The Fabricator(:private_category) after_build uses update!, which persists even under Fabricate.build. It also calls transients[:group].id, which raises if no group is passed.

verifier.reason: In spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (patch lines 716-718), the after_build block calls cat.update!(read_restricted: true), which saves the record to the database even under Fabricate.build, and it calls transients[:group].id, which raises NoMethodError on nil when no group is passed. The patch did not write this code: the new file has the same blob (a37f5b4c8b) as the old category_fabricator.rb, so the code was copied over unchanged.

findings.claim: The host validation regex's [a-z]{2,5} TLD rule rejects localhost, IP addresses and TLDs longer than 5 characters such as .museum. Migrated rows that skipped validation then fail on later edit.

verifier.reason: The regex at app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 requires a final `\.[a-z]{2,5}` label, so `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `example.museum` all fail validation. The migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:558) inserts the old setting values with raw SQL and skips validation, so those rows can't be saved again through EmbeddableHostsController#save_host (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:276).

findings.claim: Feed-polled topics now take their category from the item's host record instead of the removed embed_category setting. Items from unregistered hosts get a nil category, and admins can no longer set the feed import category.

verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-43 now passes `category: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id)` where it used to pass SiteSetting.embed_category. PollFeed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:39) calls this path, so feed items from a host with no EmbeddableHost row get a nil category, and config/site_settings.yml plus the migration delete embed_category. One caveat: admins can still choose a category per host in the new Embedding admin screen, so only the separate feed-wide setting is gone.

findings.claim: Spec files contain extra blank lines that violate RuboCop Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody.

verifier.reason: The new spec files leave blank lines just inside their block bodies, for example spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:4 and :8, spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb:4, :39 and :41, and spec/models/topic_spec.rb right after `describe "expandable_first_post?" do` and before its closing `end`. RuboCop's default Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody would flag these, but the repo has no .rubocop.yml and no rubocop in Gemfile, so nothing enforces the rule, and existing specs such as site_setting_spec.rb already use this style.

findings.claim: The singleton embedding record is fetched with store.find without an id, which resolves to a collection.

verifier.reason: In store.js.es6:64-72, `find` returns a result set only when `typeof findArgs === "object"`. When `store.find('embedding')` is called with no id, `findArgs` is undefined, so the code takes the `_hydrate(type, result['embedding'], result)` branch and builds one record. The custom adapter (admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6:4-6) points at the singleton endpoint `/admin/customize/embedding`, so this is not a collection.

findings.claim: In obj[pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [], the || [] is dead code because map always returns an array.

verifier.reason: At app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197-200, `hydrated` is the result of `obj[k].map(...)`. That result is always an array, and arrays are truthy even when empty. If `obj[k]` is null or undefined, the `.map` call throws before reaching the `||`, so `|| []` can never take effect.

findings.claim: The migration's create_table uses force: true, which drops an existing table on re-run.

verifier.reason: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 (patch line 536), the patch calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. With `force: true`, Rails drops any existing embeddable_hosts table before creating it, so its rows would be lost if the migration ran again. Rails records applied migrations in schema_migrations, so this only happens if that record is reset or the migration is run by hand.

findings.claim: before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff duplicates filters already declared by the parent Admin::AdminController.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/admin_controller.rb:3-4 already declares `before_filter :ensure_logged_in` and `before_filter :ensure_staff`. The patch's new subclasses repeat them: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController (patch line 252) and Admin::EmbeddingController (patch line 292). Rails drops a callback that is declared twice, so the repeat is redundant but harmless.

findings.claim: There is no unique index or uniqueness validation on host. With duplicate hosts, record_for_host's .first picks a category arbitrarily.

verifier.reason: The migration creates embeddable_hosts with no unique index on host (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-7), and the model only checks the host's format (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2). So the admin controller can save duplicate hosts, and record_for_host's `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no order (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) returns whichever row comes first, and that row's category is used in topic_embed.rb.
